checks.summary: Fresh official-SDK stdio discovery exposed exactly the two frozen public tools with machine-readable object input and output schemas.
Fresh live-browser discovery returned the exact mirror identity, 28 models, supported backgrounds, aspect ratios, defaults, and bounds.
Fresh solid and mesh jobs applied materially different device, background, aspect, scale, and position presets through the browser and used Dresser download events.
Both fresh PNGs exist below the fixed output root, have valid signatures, non-zero sizes, matching SHA-256 values and dimensions, and visually reflect their presets.
Fresh sequential solid and mesh jobs had unique paths and hashes, and an overlapping call received stable BUSY while its winner completed.
A real controlled-browser export timeout caused an unhandled DOWNLOAD_FAILED rejection and terminated Node instead of returning a bounded MCP error.
checks.reason: The timeout-bearing download promise can reject before exportPng attaches its await handler, so the required bounded error path is not preserved.

checks.summary: Normal privacy checks passed, but the timeout crash bypassed final cleanup and left the verifier-created mirror process listening on loopback.
checks.reason: Process termination prevents the render finally block from closing the live session, and a real orphan mirror was observed.

checks.summary: The exact mirror manifest and existing interactive route remain intact; task production files stay within the frozen package/server scope.
Fresh full lint reproduced exactly 10 errors in the same five frozen out-of-scope files and no MCP-owned error.
Production changes remain bounded to approved package metadata and server/mockup-mcp; unrelated dirty work, mirror files, portfolio UI, deployment, and Git state were not mutated.
Normal MCP contract behavior passes, but an export timeout can terminate the server process rather than return the frozen bounded error.

checks.summary: Normal controlled-browser integration passes, but the timeout failure leaves its loopback mirror process alive after Node termination.

checks.summary: Fresh public errors and stderr did not disclose source identity or executable paths, browser traffic stayed local, and no media payload logging was found.

findings.summary: The live Dresser export timeout can reject before a handler is attached, terminating Node and leaving the mirror process instead of returning a bounded MCP error.
The timeout/download negative test replaces launch with an immediate throw, so it never executes the real export timeout or cleanup branch.

debt: Ten unchanged out-of-scope full-repository lint errors remain as frozen accepted MVP debt.
The checkout contains unrelated user-owned dirty changes; the task is intentionally local-only with no authorized commit or push.
